description: Registry of external sources that may be supplied to threat-model prompt pack v3. The registry identifies each source and its permitted role. It is not a combined threat database, and presence here does not establish that a source was checked in a run.

run_contract.rule: A run may cite only entries present in its source_manifest. Every mapping must bind an external id to inventory referents and evidence. Catalog coverage is limited to the pinned inputs and is never a threat-completeness claim.

integration_modes.embedded-vocabulary: Small stable identifiers or locally maintained crosswalk rows may be passed with the prompt pack.
integration_modes.pinned-mirror: Use a release or commit-pinned source artifact and record its hash.
integration_modes.fetch-and-cache: Query only for identified components or records, then retain the response and hash used by the run.
integration_modes.reference-only: Record the canonical source and version without copying its source text.

sources.name: SRF AI threat-to-accountability crosswalk
sources.binding_rule: Use only after a system-bound threat exists. This source assigns SRF layer and accountability; it does not define threat completeness or severity.

sources.name: Common Attack Pattern Enumeration and Classification
sources.binding_rule: Bind an attack pattern to a concrete scenario, inventory referent, precondition, and asset. A CAPEC category match alone is insufficient.

sources.name: MITRE ATT&CK
sources.binding_rule: Treat ATT&CK as observed adversary behavior. Do not use an ATT&CK technique as proof of a design weakness or affected product.

sources.name: MITRE ATLAS
sources.binding_rule: Bind ATLAS behavior to a represented AI component or AI-to-traditional path and retain the pinned ATLAS release.

sources.name: OWASP AI Exchange
sources.binding_rule: Treat a slug as a locator. Record the source commit or snapshot because the guide changes without a numbered release.

sources.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
sources.binding_rule: Use a year-qualified id and title. A Top 10 category is broader than a system-specific threat unless evidence supports a narrower relation.

sources.name: Common Weakness Enumeration
sources.binding_rule: Map only an allowed weakness-level entry using root-cause evidence. Do not report a CWE category or view as a vulnerability instance.

sources.name: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures
sources.binding_rule: Require supplier, product, version, component reference, and applicability evidence. Product-name similarity is not enough.

sources.name: National Vulnerability Database
sources.binding_rule: Keep CNA and NVD provenance distinct. Bind CPE and version-range evidence to an inventory component before claiming affected status.

sources.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
sources.binding_rule: Join by an applicable CVE. KEV establishes reported exploitation of that CVE; it does not establish that the represented component is affected.

sources.name: NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 threat sources and events
sources.binding_rule: Use adversarial, accidental, structural, and environmental classes as prompts. Do not convert every appendix example into a threat.

sources.name: BSI IT-Grundschutz elementary threats
sources.authority: German Federal Office for Information Security
sources.binding_rule: Reference the applicable published edition. Record considered, applicable, or not applicable with a reason; the elementary threats are not exhaustive.
